ut.title: Ultrasonic Thickness Testing & UT Inspection | Tucson, AZ
ut.description: Ultrasonic testing in Tucson, AZ: thickness surveys and weld UT on tanks, vessels, piping and defense-plant steel, mobilized to your site. Request a quote.
ut.h1: Ultrasonic Testing (UT) and Thickness Inspection in Tucson, Arizona
ut.html:
Atlantis NDT performs ultrasonic thickness testing and ultrasonic weld inspection in Tucson, Arizona, for process piping, storage tanks, pressure vessels, boilers, water-system steel and heavy fabrications at manufacturing plants, aircraft-support facilities and utility sites across the Tucson basin. Technicians travel to your site with calibrated flaw detectors and thickness gauges, work to a written procedure and report every reading against the limit you name. To scope a job, use the Tucson UT inspection quote request and we reply within one business day.

Where ultrasonic testing is used in Tucson

Tucson is not a refinery town, and that shapes the work. The region is known for guided missile and defense manufacturing, aircraft maintenance and storage in the dry air east and northwest of the city, a university research base, and a strong optics industry. Behind every one of those sit utilities and plant systems that corrode quietly: chilled water loops, compressed air headers, steam and condensate lines, fuel storage, and the large steel tanks that hold water and treatment chemicals.

Ultrasonic thickness readings are how a facilities group in this market decides whether a section of pipe or a tank floor still has margin. A condensate return line in a manufacturing plant, a cooling-tower basin riser, a boiler blowdown line and a diesel day tank each lose wall differently, and the survey has to follow the way each one fails rather than a generic grid.

Weld examination is the second use. Fabrication shops in southern Arizona build structural frames, platforms, pressure skids, test stands and ground-support equipment, and a groove weld in thick plate may need a volumetric check that surface methods cannot give. Ultrasonic weld inspection fills that need where the construction code allows it. Tucson also sits on a major interstate corridor with steel overpasses and a railroad mainline, so structural steel and rail-served industrial yards add to the list of places a technician is asked to examine thickness or welds.

Atlantis has no office in Tucson. Crews are mobilized to the site, which means travel, lodging and plant badging are part of planning a Tucson job rather than something assumed to be around the corner.

What UT finds and what it misses

Ultrasonic testing sends sound into the material through a liquid couplant and times the echo. For thickness, the instrument measures the transit time between the probe face and the back wall and converts it to a distance using the sound velocity of the material. For welds, an angled probe sends shear waves across the joint and the technician watches for reflections from flaws.

The method is strong at wall loss on one side of steel that can be reached from the other, at laminations in plate, and at planar flaws such as lack of fusion and cracks in a weld volume. It is weak where the surface is rough or heavily scaled, where coupling is poor, and where the coarse structure of cast or austenitic material scatters the beam. Isolated pitting is the classic limit of a thickness grid: a gauge sees what is under the probe, so a pit between grid points is missed unless the scan density is raised.

In Tucson, two local conditions matter. Dust and desert grit sit on exterior steel and have to be cleaned off before a probe can couple. Stainless piping used in clean-process and water-treatment systems needs the right velocity setting and a technique suited to its grain structure, because calibrating on carbon steel and measuring stainless gives a wrong thickness. Both points are handled in the procedure before the first reading, not discovered afterward.

Codes and acceptance criteria for Tucson work

The code that governs the job decides how the examination is done and what a reading or indication means. For pressure vessels and tanks the owner usually works to API 510 or API 653, and the owner's authorized inspector is the inspector of record; Atlantis performs the examination and reports the data, such as thickness at each condition monitoring location, for that inspector to evaluate. Process piping examined under ASME B31.3 or API 570 follows the same split of roles. Weld examination on pressure equipment refers to ASME Section VIII Division 1 Appendix 12 or ASME Section V Article 4, and structural work refers to AWS D1.1 or, for highway bridges, AWS D1.5.

Thickness work is typically built on ASTM E797 and on ASME Section V Article 5 and Article 23, which carries the contact pulse-echo thickness standard. Our guide to Article 5 thickness requirements walks through what a procedure for these surveys must contain.

Arizona's own regime is narrower than many readers expect. The state's boiler safety section covers boilers and certain heaters, and since 2017 the required inspections are carried out by insurance-company or authorized contract inspectors rather than state staff. Pressure vessels that are not part of that program are governed by the owner's insurer, internal standards and OSHA process safety rules where they apply. Under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119(j), a covered facility has to inspect and test its equipment following recognized and generally accepted good engineering practice, and ultrasonic thickness data is a common part of that record.

How the work is done

A thickness job starts with the drawing or isometric and the CML list. Each location is cleaned, marked and measured, and the readings are tied to a numbering scheme that the owner can trend from one outage to the next. The gauge is calibrated on a step block of the same material before the first reading and checked again during and after the job. On corroded or pitted surfaces a dual-element probe is used, with the A-scan display on so the technician sees the echo shape and does not accept a doubled or false reading on thin wall.

Hot lines are common in plants here, and a standard probe and couplant will not survive them. High-temperature probes and couplant are used, the surface temperature is recorded, and the reading is corrected as the procedure requires. Where a line cannot be measured safely while in service, the plan changes rather than the safety rules.

Weld examination uses angle-beam probes, normally at 45, 60 or 70 degrees depending on thickness and joint geometry. A reference level or distance-amplitude curve is built from side-drilled holes in a reference block, the weld is scanned from both sides where access allows, and indications are evaluated against the acceptance table of the governing code. The technician records location along the weld, depth, length and amplitude relative to the reference.

Who does the work

Ultrasonic examinations are performed by technicians qualified under Atlantis's written practice to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. A Level II technician sets up and calibrates the equipment and performs and interprets the examination. An ASNT Level III approves the written procedure and reviews the reports. Our founder, Anoop Rayavarapu, is ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. If your site requires a customer-specific procedure, we work to it or have the Level III reconcile it with the code before mobilization. Owners that want to set up their own written practice can start with our written practice development service and the Level III consulting page.

What the Tucson UT report contains

  • Component identification, line or vessel number, drawing reference and the examined area.
  • Procedure number and revision, the governing code and edition, and the acceptance criteria applied.
  • Instrument, probe, couplant, calibration block and calibration check records.
  • Technician name and qualification level, and the date of each examination.
  • For thickness: a grid or CML table with nominal, previous and current readings, and any location at or below the minimum required thickness flagged.
  • For welds: weld identification, scan plan, each indication with position, length, depth and amplitude, and an accept or reject result.
  • Sketches or marked-up drawings where they help the owner's inspector.

Planning a UT job in Tucson

Summer heat drives most of the planning. Steel in direct sun in this basin gets hot enough to burn a hand and to change couplant behavior, so work on exterior piping and tank shells is usually scheduled for the cooler part of the day, and the surface temperature is logged. Hot surfaces also change the sound velocity slightly, which is why the correction step exists. The summer monsoon brings sudden storms, wet steel and blowing dust, and a job on an exposed structure can pause for weather.

Winters are mild compared with most industrial regions, so cold-weather couplant and gauge limits seldom apply, though high-desert nights can drop low enough to matter for equipment left on a site overnight. Defense and aerospace sites need badging and escort lead time, and they may restrict instruments, photographs and electronics, so tell us the site rules when you ask for a quote. Plant outage windows, tank cleanouts and water-system shutdowns are the points when access is best; the closer the survey is to a planned outage, the more of the asset can be measured.

Because the team travels to Tucson, scope the job as a package: how many CMLs or welds, what access equipment exists, and what the owner's inspector needs for the next decision.

UT, MT or PT for your Tucson job

Choose by the question being asked. If it is how much wall is left, or whether a weld has internal flaws, ultrasonic testing is the tool. If it is whether a carbon-steel weld or a structural casting has a surface crack, magnetic particle inspection in Tucson is faster and more sensitive at the surface. If the material is stainless, aluminum or another non-magnetic metal, liquid penetrant testing in Tucson covers surface-breaking flaws. Many jobs use two of them together: UT for the volume of a repair weld and MT or PT for the finished surface. More background is in the ultrasonic testing guide and on the national ultrasonic testing page, and the Arizona inspection services hub lists the other work we take on in the state.

Training your own UT technicians

If your plant has a standing need for thickness readings, an in-house technician can pay off. Atlantis teaches UT Level 1 and UT Level 2 theory, with hands-on practice through the UT simulator, and the employer certifies its own people under its written practice. Check SNT-TC-1A eligibility before you enroll, and see our NDT training page for Tucson for how delivery works for a Tucson employer.

faq.q: Do you provide ultrasonic thickness testing in Tucson, Arizona?
faq.a: Yes. Technicians are mobilized to Tucson plants, tank farms and fabrication shops to take thickness readings on piping, tanks, vessels and structural steel, then report them against your CML numbering and minimum thickness values.

faq.q: Does Atlantis have an office in Tucson?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no office in Tucson. Technicians travel to your site for the agreed scope, so travel, lodging and plant badging are planned into the job from the first conversation.

faq.q: Can UT replace radiography on a weld in Tucson?
faq.a: Only where the construction code and the owner permit it. Ultrasonic examination of welds is allowed by some codes, but the substitution is agreed beforehand with the owner, the engineer and any authorized inspector. Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States.

faq.q: What codes do you use for ultrasonic weld inspection?
faq.a: The code named in your contract controls: ASME Section VIII Division 1 Appendix 12 or Section V Article 4 for pressure equipment, ASME B31.3 for process piping, AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for highway bridges.

faq.q: How hot can a surface be for ultrasonic thickness readings?
faq.a: Standard probes and couplant have low limits. For hot lines the procedure calls for high-temperature probes and couplant, and the surface temperature is recorded so the reading can be corrected. Very hot lines may be measured during an outage instead.

faq.q: Will you evaluate remaining life or fitness for service?
faq.a: No. Atlantis reports the examination data. Remaining-life calculations and repair decisions belong to the owner's inspector or engineer, including the authorized inspector under API 510, API 570 or API 653.

faq.q: What do I need to send to get a UT quote for a Tucson site?
faq.a: Send the asset list or drawings, the number of thickness locations or welds, the governing code, access conditions, surface temperatures and any site badging rules. A short scope like this lets us mobilize the right technician and equipment.

faq.q: Can my own technicians learn ultrasonic testing through Atlantis?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis offers UT Level 1 and Level 2 training with simulator practice. Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies its technicians after training, experience and examination, using the written practice you adopt.

mt.title: Magnetic Particle Inspection (MPI) in Tucson, AZ | MT
mt.description: Magnetic particle inspection in Tucson, AZ: mag particle testing of welds, castings, forgings and structural steel at your site. Request an MT quote.
mt.h1: Magnetic Particle Inspection (MT) in Tucson, Arizona
mt.html:
Atlantis NDT performs magnetic particle inspection (MT) in Tucson, Arizona, on welds, castings, forgings, shafts, lifting hardware and structural steel in manufacturing plants, fabrication shops and maintenance yards. Technicians are mobilized to your site with yokes, particle suspensions, UV-A lights and field indicators, work to a written procedure and report each indication against the code or drawing you name. Send the scope through the Tucson MT inspection quote request and we reply within one business day.

Where magnetic particle inspection is used in Tucson

Southern Arizona has a specific mix of ferromagnetic steel in service: defense-contract tooling and fixtures, ground-support equipment for aircraft, structural frames and platforms built by regional fabricators, rolling stock and railroad hardware on the mainline through town, and heavy equipment that serves the state's mining and construction industries. Each category has welds and highly stressed parts that fatigue from the surface, which is exactly what mag particle testing is built to find.

Typical Tucson requests include crack checks on the welds of load-bearing fixtures, inspection of lifting lugs and spreader bars before a heavy lift, examination of shafts and pins on pumps and fans in water and power systems, and post-repair checks on weld-repaired castings. Structural steel for the highway and railroad crossings around the city adds welded connection checks to the list. Tooling that carries a missile body or a heavy assembly is not a place to leave a weld crack undiscovered.

Aircraft maintenance in the dry climate near Tucson mostly follows aircraft-specific manuals and approved procedures. Where a facility asks for MT on ground equipment, jacks, stands or hangar steel, the same field method applies, and the customer's own procedure is followed or reconciled by our Level III. Atlantis has no office in Tucson, so every job is a mobilization to your facility.

What magnetic particle inspection finds and what it misses

MT works because a crack in magnetized steel disturbs the field and forces flux out of the part, where fine iron particles gather into a visible line. It finds surface-breaking cracks and some that sit just under the surface, including fatigue cracks, grinding cracks, seams, laps and lack of fusion at the toe of a weld.

The limits come straight from the physics. The part must be ferromagnetic, so carbon and low-alloy steels and most martensitic grades are fine, while austenitic stainless steel, aluminum, copper alloys and titanium cannot be examined this way. A flaw is detected best when it lies across the magnetic field, which is why two examinations with the field turned about ninety degrees are required. Thick paint, plating and scale reduce sensitivity, and deep subsurface flaws are not reliably seen.

Arizona's intense sunlight is a practical problem for fluorescent work, since the UV-A inspection needs a darkened area. Outdoors in Tucson that usually means a shade tent or working at dusk, and visible-light particles are used instead when a procedure allows it and the contrast against the surface is adequate. The right choice is written into the procedure before the job.

Codes and acceptance criteria

Most MT in industrial plants follows ASME Section V Article 7 for the method, with acceptance from the construction code. ASME Section VIII Division 1 Mandatory Appendix 6 gives both methods and acceptance for pressure vessels, ASME B31.3 paragraph 344.3 covers process piping, and AWS D1.1 sets visual and magnetic particle criteria for structural welds. ASTM E709 is the guide behind many procedures and ASTM E1444 is the practice used for the examination itself. Our Article 7 explainer and the complete MT guide cover the requirements in more detail.

For repair and alteration work on boilers and pressure vessels in Arizona, the National Board Inspection Code and the state's boiler safety rules apply to boilers within the state program, and weld repairs on them must be carried out by an organization holding the National Board R stamp. When MT is part of such a repair, the examination is witnessed or reviewed as the inspector requires. Under API 510, 570 and 653 the owner's authorized inspector remains responsible; Atlantis performs the examination and reports the indications.

How the work is done

An AC yoke is the workhorse for field work. Its legs are placed on either side of the area, the pole spacing is set, and particles are applied while the field is on. The yoke must demonstrate its lifting power at the spacing used, and the procedure records the check. Contact prods are used only where the procedure allows them and arc burns on the part are not acceptable, so prods are rarely first choice on finished surfaces.

Wet fluorescent particles give the highest sensitivity on a clean surface. Dry powder is useful on rough welds and hot work in the field. In either case the surface is cleaned first, the particle suspension is checked with a settling test, and a pie gauge or a similar field indicator shows that the field strength and direction are adequate. After the examination, parts that will be machined, welded or placed in rotating service may need demagnetization, and a field meter confirms the residual level.

Indications are classified as relevant, non-relevant or false. A magnetic writing from a change in section, for example, is non-relevant, and the technician has to be able to explain why. Relevant indications are measured, located and compared against the acceptance criteria.

Who does the work

MT technicians are qualified under Atlantis's written practice to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. A Level II technician sets up the equipment, performs the examination and interprets the results, while an ASNT Level III approves the procedure and reviews reports. The reviewing Level III on our side is Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. If your company needs its own written practice for MT, our Level III consulting team can write or review it.

What the Tucson MT report contains

  • Part or weld identification, drawing and location, and the surface condition at examination.
  • Procedure number, revision, governing code, edition and the acceptance criteria applied.
  • Equipment: yoke or coil, lifting-power check, particle type and color, suspension concentration, UV-A intensity and white-light level where fluorescent.
  • Technician name, level and examination date.
  • Each indication with position, length and orientation, and an accept or reject result.
  • Photographs or sketches that show where the indications sit.
  • Demagnetization performed and residual field measured, when required.

Planning an MT job in Tucson

Surface temperature is the main scheduling question. Wet particle suspensions work within limited temperature ranges, and steel left in the Arizona sun can exceed what a standard procedure allows, so hot components are shaded, allowed to cool or examined with a qualified high-temperature technique. Monsoon storms and wind-blown dust interfere with particle application outdoors, and a job in the open can need a windbreak or a rain day.

Defense and aerospace sites require badging, and some restrict the equipment that can be carried in, including lights, tablets and phones, so share those rules at the quote stage. For fabrication shops, the best time for MT is after the weld has cooled and before paint or coating goes on, because coatings reduce sensitivity and then have to be removed again. Request the examination as part of the shop schedule so that the crew can mobilize when the work is ready.

MT, PT or UT for your Tucson job

For a ferromagnetic weld where the concern is a surface crack, MT is usually the most sensitive and quickest field method. If the metal is non-magnetic, use liquid penetrant testing in Tucson. If the question is internal flaws or remaining wall, ultrasonic testing in Tucson is the better fit. The comparison in MT versus PT goes through the trade-offs, and the national magnetic particle testing page lists what Atlantis offers across the country. Work in other Arizona cities is covered in the Arizona inspection services hub.

Training your own MT technicians

A fabrication shop or maintenance group that runs MT every week may want trained people of its own. Atlantis offers MT Level 1 and MT Level 2 training; the employer certifies under its written practice after the candidate meets training, experience and examination requirements. See NDT training in Tucson for how courses are delivered to Tucson employers.

faq.q: Do you offer magnetic particle inspection in Tucson, AZ?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis mobilizes MT technicians to Tucson fabrication shops, plants and yards to inspect welds, castings, forgings and structural steel using yokes and wet or dry particles, and reports each indication against your code.

faq.q: Can magnetic particle testing be used on stainless steel or aluminum?
faq.a: Not on austenitic stainless steel, aluminum, copper alloys or titanium, because they are not ferromagnetic. For those metals the surface-breaking crack check is done with liquid penetrant testing instead.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis lab or office in Tucson?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no office in Tucson. Technicians travel to the site where the part or weld is located, so plan for mobilization, badging and any site safety orientation.

faq.q: Can MT be done outdoors in Arizona sunlight?
faq.a: Yes, with the right setup. Fluorescent particles need a darkened area, so a shade tent or working at dusk is used, while visible-light particles can work in daylight when the procedure allows and contrast is adequate.

faq.q: What standard governs magnetic particle inspection?
faq.a: ASME Section V Article 7 is the usual method standard, with acceptance criteria from the construction code such as ASME Section VIII Division 1 Appendix 6, ASME B31.3 or AWS D1.1. ASTM E1444 and E709 support the procedure.

faq.q: Do parts need demagnetizing after MT?
faq.a: Often. Demagnetization is needed when residual magnetism could interfere with later welding, machining, instruments or rotating service. The procedure states the requirement and a field meter confirms the residual level where required.

faq.q: How do I request an MT quote for a Tucson job?
faq.a: Use the quote request link on this page and send part descriptions, quantities, material, code and acceptance criteria, surface condition and site access rules. We reply within one business day to confirm scope.

faq.q: Can my staff be trained in magnetic particle testing?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis offers MT Level 1 and Level 2 training. Your employer certifies technicians under the company written practice, which follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A, after training, experience and examination.

pt.title: Dye Penetrant Inspection (PT) in Tucson, AZ | Liquid Penetrant
pt.description: Liquid penetrant testing in Tucson, AZ: dye penetrant inspection of welds, castings, aluminum and stainless parts at your site. Request a PT quote.
pt.h1: Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT) and Dye Penetrant Inspection in Tucson, Arizona
pt.html:
Atlantis NDT performs liquid penetrant testing, also called dye penetrant inspection or PT, in Tucson, Arizona, on welds, castings, machined parts and fabricated assemblies in stainless steel, aluminum, nickel alloys and carbon steel. Technicians travel to your plant or shop with qualified materials and written procedures, and report every indication against your specification. Describe the parts in the Tucson PT inspection quote request and we reply within one business day.

Where liquid penetrant testing is used in Tucson

PT is the method for the materials that magnetic particle inspection cannot touch, and Tucson has plenty of them. Aerospace and defense manufacturing in the region uses aluminum, titanium and stainless alloys; clean-process and water-treatment plants use stainless piping and vessels; food and beverage producers use sanitary stainless tubing; and optics and instrument makers machine non-magnetic housings and frames. A crack in any of these starts at the surface, so a method that draws penetrant into the opening is exactly what is needed.

Common Tucson requests include weld checks on stainless process piping, inspection of aluminum fabrications and fixtures, examination of machined and cast components for cracks and porosity open to the surface, and post-repair checks on pressure-boundary welds before a hydrostatic test. Heat exchangers and boiler tubing in commercial buildings and plants can need surface checks on welded attachments after repair.

Atlantis has no office in Tucson. We mobilize technicians to your site, and for shop work we ask that the parts be accessible, clean and ready when the crew arrives.

What PT finds and what it misses

PT reveals only discontinuities that are open to the surface. The penetrant is drawn into a crack, pore or lap by capillary action, the excess is removed, and a developer pulls the trapped liquid back out so that the flaw shows as a bright line or spot against the background. It works on any non-porous material, magnetic or not, which is why it is the standard answer for stainless steel, aluminum and nickel alloys.

Its limits are as important. A flaw that does not break the surface cannot be found, and a flaw whose opening is filled with oxide, paint, oil, blasting debris or smeared metal gives no indication. Grinding, peening and machining can close surface openings, so etching may be required before penetrant is applied. Porous materials absorb penetrant and produce a background that hides everything.

Surface preparation therefore decides the quality of a PT job more than any other factor. In Tucson the usual contaminants are dust, fine sand, cutting fluid, and the sealers that are applied to exterior steel and aluminum in strong sun. These are cleaned off as the procedure directs, and the cleaning method is chosen to avoid forcing contamination into the flaw.

Codes and acceptance criteria

ASME Section V Article 6 is the method standard for most industrial PT. Acceptance comes from the construction code: ASME Section VIII Division 1 Mandatory Appendix 8 for pressure vessels, ASME B31.3 paragraph 344.4 with Table 341.3.2 for process piping, and AWS D1.1 for structural welds in steel. ASTM E165 is the practice commonly cited in general industry. Our Article 6 explainer covers materials, dwell and developer requirements.

Penetrant materials for work on nickel alloys, austenitic stainless steel and titanium have to meet low sulfur, halogen and sodium content limits, because those elements can damage the alloy. The procedure names the material lot and the contaminant check, and the records show it. For pressure equipment under API 510, API 570 or API 653 the owner's authorized inspector stays responsible; Atlantis performs the examination and reports what it finds. Arizona's boiler rules govern boilers and certain heaters, and weld repairs on them go through National Board R-stamp organizations, so PT after such a repair is performed to the repair plan the inspector accepted.

How the work is done

The sequence is the same every time and each step has a purpose. The surface is cleaned and dried, penetrant is applied by spray or brush and left to dwell for the time the procedure specifies, the excess is removed, developer is applied in a thin even coat, and the area is examined after the development time. Visible dye penetrant is used in normal light and is the usual field choice. Fluorescent penetrant is more sensitive and needs a darkened area and UV-A light.

Method choice follows the part. A solvent-removable visible system is portable and works for most field welds. Water-washable or post-emulsifiable systems are suited to shop work on rougher surfaces and larger batches. Developer type, dwell and removal technique are fixed in the procedure and checked by a test panel or comparator block when the code requires it. A technician who changes any of them without authority invalidates the examination.

Indications are interpreted as relevant, non-relevant or false. Bleed-out from a rough surface, a scratch or a loose residue might be non-relevant, and the technician evaluates by wiping and re-developing when the procedure allows.

Who does the work

PT technicians are qualified under Atlantis's written practice to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. A Level II technician selects and applies the materials, performs the examination and interprets the results. An ASNT Level III approves the procedure and reviews reports; the Level III is Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. Companies with their own technicians can have the written practice and procedures reviewed through written practice development and the Level III consulting page.

What the Tucson PT report contains

  • Part or weld identification, material, drawing reference and the area examined.
  • Procedure number and revision, governing code and edition, and acceptance criteria.
  • Penetrant system: type, method, manufacturer, lot numbers for cleaner, penetrant and developer, and contaminant-limit certification where required.
  • Surface temperature, dwell time and development time.
  • Technician name, level and date.
  • Each indication with location, size and shape, and an accept or reject result.
  • Photographs or sketches of rejectable indications, and the post-examination cleaning performed.

Planning a PT job in Tucson

Temperature is the planning constraint here. The standard PT range under ASME Section V is a part and material temperature between about 40 and 125 degrees Fahrenheit, and Tucson steel in summer sun is routinely hotter. Outside the range the procedure has to be qualified for the actual temperature, or the work is moved to early morning or shaded and allowed to cool. Penetrant that dries on a hot surface before dwell ends gives poor results, so sun shades and short work sections are common on exterior piping.

Monsoon humidity and storms can wet a prepared surface, and wind-blown dust can contaminate it again, so a job outdoors needs a plan for re-cleaning. Defense and aerospace sites have badging and equipment rules that can restrict chemical products on site, so confirm what penetrant systems the facility accepts. Waste handling is part of the job: solvent wipes and rags are collected and disposed of under the site's requirements.

PT, MT or UT for your Tucson job

For stainless, aluminum or other non-magnetic metal, PT is normally the right surface method. For carbon steel, magnetic particle inspection in Tucson is often faster and finds some subsurface flaws as well. For internal flaws and wall loss, ultrasonic testing in Tucson is the better fit. The MT versus PT comparison and the national penetrant testing page expand on the choice. The Arizona inspection services hub covers the rest of our work in the state.

Training your own PT technicians

Penetrant testing is one of the quickest methods to learn, and an in-house technician can take over routine checks. Atlantis offers PT Level 1 and PT Level 2 training, with practice on the PT simulator. The employer certifies trainees under its own written practice. Our Tucson training page explains how delivery works for local employers.
